newsitem.title: USA: NY court upholds regulators on utility competition.
newsitem.headline: NY court upholds regulators on utility competition.

text.p: The State of New York Public Service Commission said a state court Tuesday upheld the commission's authority to implement electric utility competition.

It said a ruling by Judge Harris, State Supreme Court, Albany County, denied an article 78 application by the New York State Energy Association and its utility members -- Brooklyn Union Gas Co, Long Island Lighting Co, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc, and Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp.
The group's other members are Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, Rochester Gas & Electric Corp and New York State Electric & Gas Corp.

The utilities filed the suit September 18 saying they did so to preserve their right to challenge the commission's May 20 decision that set the ground rules for future competition in New York's electric utility industry.
Energy Association and company officials were not immediately available for comment on the ruling.

Chairman John F. O'Mara said "the commission is pleased that the court upheld our authority to provide consumers more choices and lower prices through competition in the electric industry in New York as envisioned by our Competitive Opportunities Opinion."
